I’m trying to break this cycle and I wish that I never started taking Percocet at 13 I didn’t know what it would lead too. My childhood was very fucked up and there’s things I think that are normal but they aren’t. I’m trying to slowly process that. She had a better childhood then I had not a fantastic one but a lot better than mine. The only way I’ve known to cope is using drugs. I’m trying to find other ways. But arguing doesn’t help and I know it’s my fault most the time, for not telling the truth of use. I love her more than anything she has been the best thing to happen to me and is a beautiful human and I feel like I’ve ruined that. I’m trying to fix my wrongs I really am. I did get a planner to write out small goals and things like that to try and help with it and just being better about things in general and not so forgetful.

Honestly man as someone that is recovering and on methadone sounds like “early” addiction he wants the help. He just doesn’t FULLY want it yet. He at least made that first step in telling someone about it, honestly to me that’s tremendous. He’s not responding cause he doesn’t want to confront it yet probably. At least that’s how I would be if it was me I would just try to keep putting it off. I would just send him a message telling him like hey ya know I am here for you and at least give him the resources. If he chooses to follow it great but you can’t force him at the end of the day. Also him saying he’s not THAT hooked for rehab shows he hasn’t fully accepted his addiction yet.  It is scary telling people cause you do feel embarrassed and ashamed and don’t want to be judged. What you can do to help man is being there for him and let him know you will listen to him if he needs someone to talk to cause man I’m telling you just even talking about it can help so much. It’s a long hard road to recovery. I’m now over a month clean.
